title: SOFR and DVP repo volume give a bounded daily funding snapshot
dek: SOFR fell 2 basis points while preliminary DVP repo volume rose 0.05%. The paired move is context—not evidence of broad funding stress.
author: My Quant research desk
original_contribution: A two-series calculation that pairs the latest official SOFR observations with preliminary DVP repo-volume observations, while keeping the different source dates and limits explicit.
limitations: This is a two-observation snapshot with asynchronous source dates: SOFR through August 12 and preliminary DVP repo volume through August 11.
SOFR is a reference rate and does not measure every funding condition.
The DVP repo observations are preliminary and may be revised; a missing value may reflect no trading or a confidentiality edit and must not be read as zero.

sources.label: New York Fed: Secured Overnight Financing Rate
New York Fed: machine-readable SOFR observations
Office of Financial Research: Short-term Funding Monitor
Office of Financial Research: DVP outstanding repo-volume series

sections.heading: What changed
paragraphs: The latest official SOFR observation was 3.62% on August 12, down from 3.64% on August 11. That is a fall of 2 basis points.

Preliminary DVP outstanding repo volume was $3.397 trillion on August 11, up from $3.395 trillion on August 10. Using the unrounded official observations, the increase was 0.05% when rounded to two decimal places.
The dates are not synchronized: the latest SOFR observation is one day newer than the latest DVP repo-volume observation.

sections.heading: What the pair can tell us
paragraphs: Read together, the two series provide a narrow daily view of secured funding: the reference rate moved down while this measure of outstanding repo volume changed only slightly.
That combination does not establish broad funding stress. Neither series can carry that conclusion alone, and the small volume change is not a system-wide stress measure.

sections.heading: Why the interpretation stays bounded
paragraphs: SOFR is a transaction-volume-weighted median reference rate, not a complete map of funding conditions. The DVP series covers a specific repo-market segment and the latest observations are preliminary.

The defensible conclusion is therefore the snapshot itself: SOFR fell 2 basis points and preliminary DVP outstanding volume edged up 0.05% across their respective latest two observations. Anything broader needs additional, independent evidence.

sections.heading: What would invalidate this snapshot
paragraphs: A revision by either official source that changes one of the four input observations—and therefore either calculated move—would invalidate this reading.
A missing DVP value would not be evidence of zero activity. OFR notes that missingness may reflect no trading or a confidentiality disclosure edit.
